notes: Self-contained: every case runs against the committed fixture evals/fixtures/sample-ts-project, no external service. The fixture plants one genuinely dead file, one unused export, one unused exported type and one unused dependency, plus two live guardrail traps Knip still flags (a dynamic-import target and a config-referenced file). The skill's script is prompt-independent, so the three cases grade the same categorized report on different slices.

evals.name: findings
evals.prompt: Audit skills/dead-code-audit/evals/fixtures/sample-ts-project for dead code: unused files, unused exports, unused exported types and unused dependencies.
evals.expected_output: The script's categorized report verbatim: a header, the five category sections with counts, and the before/after score.
assertions: Header names the fixture and Knip, with no 'using Knip defaults' suffix (the repo has a knip.json)
The genuinely dead file src/unused-widget.ts is reported under Unused files
The planted unused export buildLegacyUrl is reported with its file:line
The planted unused exported type DeprecatedPayload is reported with its file:line
The planted unused dependency left-pad is reported, count 1
Every one of the five category sections is present

evals.name: score
evals.prompt: Run the dead-code audit on skills/dead-code-audit/evals/fixtures/sample-ts-project and tell me the before/after score: how many lines and dependencies I could remove.
evals.expected_output: The script's before/after score block, with the removable-LOC and unused-dependency numbers measured on the committed fixture.
assertions: The score block frames its numbers as candidates to verify against the guardrails
Removable lines of code equal the planted 18 across 3 unused files
The unused-dependency count equals the planted 1
The score's file count (3) agrees with the Unused files section count (3)

evals.name: guardrails
evals.prompt: Find the dead code in skills/dead-code-audit/evals/fixtures/sample-ts-project, but watch for false positives — which findings are actually safe to delete?
evals.expected_output: The script's categorized report. Knip surfaces the two live traps as unused-file candidates; ruling them out is the agent's documented judgment step, not the script's job.
assertions: The dynamic-import target src/plugins/plugin-a.ts is surfaced as an unused-file candidate
The config-referenced file src/registry.ts is surfaced as an unused-file candidate
The script frames the findings as candidates to verify, not as verdicts
The genuinely dead file sits in the same undifferentiated candidate list as the two traps
